requirements.description: Implement the approved source proposal:mechanics. The complete source is supplied in the manifest.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns on the baseplate as an R6 character and sees a stationary target dummy a few studs ahead. Left-clicking (mouse button 1, ignored when the click is over UI) plays the attached R6 punch animation on the player's character. A punch counts as a hit when the dummy is within punch reach of the player's character during the swing. A simple on-screen counter goes up by exactly one for each hit.

Hit rule: the client sends a punch request to the server. The server validates it: the character is alive, the punch cooldown has elapsed, and the dummy is within roughly 6 studs and in front of the character. If the request is valid, the server registers one hit and updates that player's counter. Each swing can score at most one hit, and the player cannot start a new punch until the current animation finishes. A swing that misses plays the animation but does not change the counter.

Counter: a per-player HUD number, starting at 0, that increases by 1 on each valid hit and resets when the player rejoins. There is no win state, timer, health bar, score saving or other mechanic beyond what was asked.

Input: PC only, keyboard and mouse. Left click is the punch button. There are no touch, gamepad or console controls.

Exclusions: no sound effects and no visual effects on punch, hit or the counter. Any sounds or particle/visual effects embedded in the attached assets must be disabled or removed to honor this. The attached punch asset is retained as animation source data. The R6 rig is used only with a matching R6 animation.

Asset reuse: the attached Target Dummy (which contains scripts) and the attached punch animation model are used as selected. Inspect their included scripts and animation instances before writing any glue. Only the missing integration is authored: click input, hit validation and the counter.
Reach is about 6 studs from the character's root part to the dummy, with the dummy roughly in front of the player.
The hit is registered when the swing starts, without waiting for a specific animation keyframe, and the swing cooldown equals the animation length. If the animation exposes a marker, the hit is timed to it.
A hit counts whether or not the dummy's own scripts react. The dummy's health and respawn behavior is kept only if it does not add visual or sound effects and does not interfere with the counter.
The counter is per player and not saved between sessions.
Click-and-hold does not auto-repeat. Each click is one punch.
The punch animation is played at normal action priority on the local player's R6 Animator.
requirements.acceptance: The implementation satisfies proposal:mechanics, including its saved decisions and limits. Native behavior still requires a Studio test.

requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimal training-yard look: a plain, readable practice arena with no story. The tan or red dummy is the focal point and stands out clearly against the gray baseplate. The HUD is a small, clean counter in a screen corner, for example the label 'Hits' with a large number, with high-contrast white text on a dark semi-transparent panel so it reads at a glance. No sounds, particles, flashes, camera shake or other feedback beyond the punch animation and the counter number changing.
The default template sky and lighting stay unchanged, with no mood lighting.
The counter changes only its number, with no animation or tween, to respect 'no visual effects'.

requirements.sourceQuote:
Use the existing baseplate (top at y=0) as the only ground. Do not add a floor, walls, ceiling or platforms, and do not change lighting, sky or atmosphere.

Layout: the default spawn is near the origin. Place the target dummy standing on the ground about 10 studs in front of the spawn, facing the spawn, so it is visible immediately. The player walks up to about 3-5 studs from the dummy and punches. Leave open space around the dummy so the player can walk around it. The dummy is anchored or otherwise stationary and does not move or attack.

HUD: a ScreenGui with one counter label at the top center or top-left. It is sized for a PC screen, does not block the view of the dummy and has no mobile layout.
The dummy is placed at roughly (0, 0, -10), standing on the ground.
No extra props, decorations or fences are added.

requirements.description: Implement the approved source proposal:mechanics. The complete source is supplied in the manifest.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns on the baseplate as an R6 character and sees a stationary target dummy a few studs ahead. Left-clicking (mouse button 1, ignored when the click is over UI) plays the attached R6 punch animation on the player's character. A punch counts as a hit when the dummy is within punch reach of the player's character during the swing. A simple on-screen counter goes up by exactly one for each hit.

Hit rule: the client sends a punch request to the server. The server validates it: the character is alive, the punch cooldown has elapsed, and the dummy is within roughly 6 studs and in front of the character. If the request is valid, the server registers one hit and updates that player's counter. Each swing can score at most one hit, and the player cannot start a new punch until the current animation finishes. A swing that misses plays the animation but does not change the counter.

Counter: a per-player HUD number, starting at 0, that increases by 1 on each valid hit and resets when the player rejoins. There is no win state, timer, health bar, score saving or other mechanic beyond what was asked.

Input: PC only, keyboard and mouse. Left click is the punch button. There are no touch, gamepad or console controls.

Exclusions: no sound effects and no visual effects on punch, hit or the counter. Any sounds or particle/visual effects embedded in the attached assets must be disabled or removed to honor this. The attached punch asset is retained as animation source data. The R6 rig is used only with a matching R6 animation.

Asset reuse: the attached Target Dummy (which contains scripts) and the attached punch animation model are used as selected. Inspect their included scripts and animation instances before writing any glue. Only the missing integration is authored: click input, hit validation and the counter.
Reach is about 6 studs from the character's root part to the dummy, with the dummy roughly in front of the player.
The hit is registered when the swing starts, without waiting for a specific animation keyframe, and the swing cooldown equals the animation length. If the animation exposes a marker, the hit is timed to it.
A hit counts whether or not the dummy's own scripts react. The dummy's health and respawn behavior is kept only if it does not add visual or sound effects and does not interfere with the counter.
The counter is per player and not saved between sessions.
Click-and-hold does not auto-repeat. Each click is one punch.
The punch animation is played at normal action priority on the local player's R6 Animator.
requirements.acceptance: The implementation satisfies proposal:mechanics, including its saved decisions and limits. Native behavior still requires a Studio test.

requirements.description: Implement the approved source proposal:theme. The complete source is supplied in the manifest.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimal training-yard look: a plain, readable practice arena with no story. The tan or red dummy is the focal point and stands out clearly against the gray baseplate. The HUD is a small, clean counter in a screen corner, for example the label 'Hits' with a large number, with high-contrast white text on a dark semi-transparent panel so it reads at a glance. No sounds, particles, flashes, camera shake or other feedback beyond the punch animation and the counter number changing.
The default template sky and lighting stay unchanged, with no mood lighting.
The counter changes only its number, with no animation or tween, to respect 'no visual effects'.

requirements.description: Implement the approved source proposal:environment. The complete source is supplied in the manifest.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Use the existing baseplate (top at y=0) as the only ground. Do not add a floor, walls, ceiling or platforms, and do not change lighting, sky or atmosphere.

Layout: the default spawn is near the origin. Place the target dummy standing on the ground about 10 studs in front of the spawn, facing the spawn, so it is visible immediately. The player walks up to about 3-5 studs from the dummy and punches. Leave open space around the dummy so the player can walk around it. The dummy is anchored or otherwise stationary and does not move or attack.

HUD: a ScreenGui with one counter label at the top center or top-left. It is sized for a PC screen, does not block the view of the dummy and has no mobile layout.
The dummy is placed at roughly (0, 0, -10), standing on the ground.
No extra props, decorations or fences are added.

needs.role: The user's attached stationary target dummy that the player punches, placed on the baseplate in front of spawn.
needs.constraints: Use the attached Target Dummy (Respawns) exactly as selected; do not replace or re-search it. Keep it stationary, standing on the ground at y=0, facing the spawn. Inspect its 3 scripts and hierarchy first. Keep useful existing structure such as the Humanoid or hit parts, but disable or remove any embedded sounds or visual effects (particles, flashes, highlights), since the user wants none. Its scripts must not add score or conflict with the counter. Static inspection is not gameplay verification.

intent.experienceRole: The dummy is the only target of the fighting game and the thing whose hits the counter measures.
intent.interaction: The player walks up and left-clicks. If the punch reaches the dummy, it counts as a hit and the counter goes up by 1 immediately. The dummy stays stationary and has no sound or visual reaction.
reusableFeatures: Humanoid or hit-detection parts and a primary part usable for the distance check
Existing respawn or health scripts to inspect for conflicts with hit counting
Embedded sounds or visual effects to disable
Model hierarchy and scale for placement on the baseplate

needs.role: The user's attached R6 punch animation, played when the player left-clicks. It is retained as animation source data.

If it holds several clips, use only the punch.
